description: The only thing owed by the user is the OLDEST message in the window, and eight louder, more recent messages follow it. The style failure is chronological order: a briefing that reads like a timeline buries the one actionable line at the bottom.

events.context_label: Headcount request — need your approval before the req opens
events.text: The backfill req for Amara's role is sitting in my queue and I can't open it without your approval in Workday. Recruiting has a candidate they want to move on but cannot schedule until the req is live. This has been waiting since last Monday.

Checkout returned 502s for 11 minutes this afternoon. Root cause was a connection pool exhausted by the new fraud-check call. Mitigated by raising the pool size; permanent fix is to make the call async, tracked in CHK-441.
Revenue impact was about £4,200 in abandoned carts. Finance has the number, no action needed from engineering.
Weekly pipeline: 14 applications, 3 phone screens scheduled, 1 onsite. No reqs opened this week.
Migration to the new build runners is done. Median CI time went from 11 minutes to 4. Nothing needed from anyone, just closing this out.
Design and engineering agreed to freeze the component library API for the rest of the quarter. Additive changes only. Both leads signed off.
Postmortem for the checkout 502s is written up and circulated. Three action items, all owned, all with dates. I'm not asking for review — just logging that it's done.
Dependency upgrade week is finished — 62 packages bumped, all green, no breaking changes. Closing it out.
Reminder that the office is closed Monday for the bank holiday. No on-call changes, the rota already accounts for it.

ground_truth.notes: ORDER is the failure mode, not selection. Every claim in both stored anti-patterns is true and citable, so recall, precision, citation accuracy and hallucination rate are all perfect for them — and both are unusable. The first is chronological transcription, which buries the single obligation in position one of nine equally-weighted sentences and lets eight louder items drown it. The second is subtler and more tempting: it leads with the genuinely interesting incident (an outage with a money figure) and puts the obligation last, which is what recency-and-drama ranking produces. The correct briefing leads with the Workday approval because it is the only thing that will not resolve itself, and because it has already been blocked a week. Note that the incident is objectively the more INTERESTING event and still belongs second: interesting is not the same as owed.
